Compare Clustering Methods at a Shared Number of Clusters

Source: R/Processing.R
analyze_and_save_clusters.Rd

Finds the numbers of clusters that every clustering method (pipeline) produced somewhere in its resolution sweep, so methods can be compared at the same number of clusters rather than at the same resolution value. For each method and each shared cluster number it takes the highest resolution giving that number, plots the size of the smallest cluster against the number of clusters, saves the plot, and returns the resolutions for one target number.

Usage

analyze_and_save_clusters(
  seurat_obj,
  output_dir = ".",
  plot_prefix = "min_cluster_size_plot",
  target_cluster_num = NULL,
  pipelines = NULL,
  min_cells_line = 30
)

Arguments

seurat_obj

A Seurat object whose metadata holds the cluster columns of one or more resolution sweeps.

output_dir

Character. Directory where the plot is saved (created if missing). Default is ".".

plot_prefix

Character. File-name prefix of the saved PNG; a timestamp is appended. Default is "min_cluster_size_plot".

target_cluster_num

Numeric or NULL. The number of clusters to report. Must be one of the shared cluster numbers. If NULL (default), you are asked in an interactive session; otherwise (or on invalid input) the highest shared number is used.

pipelines

Character vector or NULL. Only compare these methods (names as described above). NULL (default) uses every method found.

min_cells_line

Numeric. Height of the dashed red reference line on the plot, a warning level for clusters that are too small to interpret. Default is 30.

Value

Invisibly, a tibble with one row per method for the target number of clusters: Pipeline, Resolution (the highest resolution giving that number), Num_Clusters and Min_Cluster_Size. It is also printed. Attributes: "plot" (the ggplot), "plot_data" (the values for every shared cluster number) and "file" (path of the saved PNG). The plot is also printed in interactive sessions.

Details

Resolution columns are recognised by Seurat's naming, <graph>_res.<resolution> (e.g. from ClusterAndUMAP() or Seurat::FindClusters()). The method name is the part before .log_snn/.sct_snn for the OHMmy naming ("log.fastmnn.log_snn_res.1" -> "log.fastmnn", "sct.fastmnn.sct_snn_res.1" -> "sct.fastmnn"), and the graph name otherwise ("RNA_snn_res.0.5" -> "RNA_snn").

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Two resolution sweeps, e.g. LogNormalize and SCTransform with FastMNN
res <- analyze_and_save_clusters(
  seurat_obj         = my_seurat,     # has log.fastmnn.log_snn_res.* and sct.fastmnn.sct_snn_res.*
  output_dir         = "Plots_cluster_choice",
  target_cluster_num = 12
)
res                       # resolution of each method that gives 12 clusters
attr(res, "plot")         # smallest cluster size vs number of clusters

# Compare only some of the methods
analyze_and_save_clusters(my_seurat, pipelines = c("log.fastmnn", "log.har"))
} # }
